_why: References that resolve on a branch this tree has deliberately NOT merged.
A dangling reference is normally a defect: prose pointing at prose that
is not there.  These are a different thing -- the entry exists, it is
just on a branch being held back on purpose, so blocking the gate on
them would mean master cannot go green until somebody merges a branch
they have chosen not to merge.
THIS REGISTER GOES STALE LOUDLY, which is the whole point and is copied
from tools/gccdiverge.json.  refcheck fails if an entry here starts
RESOLVING -- because that means the branch landed and the entry is now a
lie -- exactly as it fails for a reference that dangles and is not
listed.  So this cannot rot into a permanent exemption: the day
v34-instrumentation merges, the gate demands these lines be deleted.
It is not a place to silence an inconvenient reference.  An entry needs
a branch that really contains the target and a reason a reader can

EMPTY, and kept rather than deleted: the mechanism is documented here for the next branch that has to be held.  Its first entry covered 13 findings on improve/v34-training and was removed the moment that branch merged -- the gate reported them STALE and refused, which is the property this file exists to have.  Its second covered 6701, 6900, 6901 and 6903 on v34-instrumentation, and was removed by copying those four findings onto master instead: the tools that cite them were already here, the register went red twice in three days, and a hold that keeps recurring is telling you to fix the split rather than to widen the hold.
